notes.bank: Reviewed the noun and verb splits. The sampled OEWN senses cover aircraft banking, river banks, trust, and depositing money; the Simple glosses cover riverbank and aircraft turning. Those are distinct uses, and no Simple gloss was accepted as a matched alternative, so the source senses must remain separate. Examples visibly contain the target, but the Tatoeba loan sentence is not assigned to a particular bank sense.
notes.apple: The OEWN fruit and Simple fruit gloss agree closely, and one Simple source sense is now uniquely aligned. The Big Apple proper-name use remains distinct. Food and Nature labels stay on their respective senses; no word-level category is emitted because the senses differ. Tatoeba examples remain word-level and sense-unverified.
notes.reward: The sampled OEWN senses distinguish behavior reinforcement from payment, while the Simple verb gloss describes giving something as a reward. The Tatoeba examples use the compensation sense and contain the word, but remain sense-unverified. The regression check correctly leaves reward without the Nature category.
notes.set: The many adjective, noun, and verb senses are kept apart; samples range from solidified, ready, exercise series, social group, arranging, and the past form. Simple examples support some everyday uses. This entry is unusually polysemous, so a UI must not treat the first sense as representative. Tatoeba matches are not sense-labeled.
notes.run: Reviewed noun and verb senses spanning a baseball score, election campaign, continuous performance, undoing, diffusion, and managing a place. The Simple verb gloss and inflected example agree with the management use. The large sense inventory needs sense selection in the UI; word-presence alone cannot place the Tatoeba matches.
notes.light: The sampled senses distinguish illumination, brightness, agility, low burden, warning signal, and settling. A narrow Science label applies to the electromagnetic-radiation sense only; the polysemous word has no word-level consensus category. Tatoeba examples are only word-presence checked.
notes.charge: Reviewed noun and verb samples: assignments, a person in one's care, electrical charging, and heraldic marking show substantial sense spread. The Simple electrical gloss remains separately attributed unless uniquely aligned. Emotions and Science occur only as sense labels; the word has no consensus category.
notes.lead: This spelling combines separate noun and verb meanings. OEWN samples include a card lead, a story introduction, causing an action, and producing a result; Simple also supplies the heavy-metal noun and a guiding use. These are not safe to merge without phonetic/sense evidence, and the current no-match behavior preserves that distinction.
notes.tear: The noun and verb senses cover a rip/opening and crying as well as the action of ripping. Homographs and ordinary uses remain separate; no word-level topic is assigned. Any sense label applies only to that sense, not to the whole spelling. Inflection checks do not verify meaning.
notes.present: The adjective senses cover current and being here; noun senses include tense/time; verb senses include presenting or performing. Simple glosses cover presence, current time, and showing/giving. The spelling and POS separation is useful, but pronunciation and sense display must distinguish the noun gift use from the reviewed samples rather than imply one meaning.
notes.photosynthesis: OEWN and Simple explanations both describe organisms making compounds/food using light. The generated Science topic is recorded on the relevant sense and word only under the configured consensus rule. The Simple definition remains separately attributed unless a unique alignment is accepted; Tatoeba sentences remain sense-unverified.
notes.gravity: Reviewed seriousness and physical-attraction senses; Simple supplies the seriousness meaning. Emotions and Science labels are sense-specific and the word has no consensus category. Tatoeba examples include the term but are not classified between physical and figurative uses.
notes.oxygen: The OEWN chemical-element definition and Simple breathing-gas explanation are compatible descriptions of the broad concept, while the Simple atom-of-oxygen gloss expresses a different usage and stays separate unless uniquely aligned. Science is available as a sense label; no word-level category is assigned because not enough senses support consensus. Tatoeba examples remain sense-unverified.
notes.entropy: The two OEWN noun senses explicitly separate thermodynamic unavailable energy from information-theoretic uncertainty. This is a useful technical distinction. There is no Simple alternative in this build; the Tatoeba matches are not sense-verified and no topic tag is assigned.
notes.cell: The biological unit and small-compartment senses are distinct in OEWN; Simple contributes the living-organism definition. A unique Simple-to-OEWN alignment may attach the compatible definition without collapsing other meanings. Tatoeba examples have only token/inflection checks, so they should not be presented as biology examples without manual sense assignment.
notes.molecule: OEWN separates the ordinary 'tiny piece' usage from the chemistry/physics structural unit. The Simple smallest-part gloss supports the technical concept at a learner level, but the importer did not attach it to a particular OEWN sense. Example coverage is sparse and does not establish sense fit.
notes.isotope: The OEWN definition gives the essential distinction of equal atomic number and different neutron count. The Simple gloss correctly describes same element/same proton count with different neutron count. This is one clear technical entry, though the two source definitions remain separately attributed and examples are not sense-reviewed.
notes.organism: The sampled OEWN senses distinguish an independent living thing from a system analogous to a living body. The Simple gloss is aligned in meaning with the first broad sense, but was not attached as an alternative. The example matches are presence-checked only; a Nature/Biology topic would improve coverage.
notes.quantum: OEWN's discrete physical quantity and Simple's quantum-theory gloss are related, while Simple's 'total amount' use is broader. Keeping these as source-specific senses avoids flattening technical and general uses. Seven noun senses suggest that ranking/display needs review; the sample examples are not sense-assigned.
notes.atom: OEWN separates a tiny-piece figurative use from the chemical particle; Simple supplies both a smallest-bit gloss and a subatomic-particle description. The senses should remain distinct by context. Example checks verify only occurrence, not whether the sentence is about chemistry.
notes.portent: The OEWN gloss ('a sign of something about to happen') and Simple gloss (something indicating an unusual or major event to come) are compatible. They are retained as separate source senses because the matcher did not accept an alignment. The two Tatoeba sentences contain the term but have no manual sense assignment; no unrelated topic tag is present.
notes.serendipity: OEWN and Simple both describe fortunate, valuable discoveries by chance. The Simple definition remains separately attributed because no unique alignment was accepted. The broad noun.phenomenon lexname no longer assigns Science by itself; this abstract word is left unclassified. Tatoeba presence does not prove a matching context.
notes.ephemeral: The adjective means short-lived/temporary in both OEWN and Simple. OEWN also has a noun for something short-lived, which remains distinct from the adjective. Nature appears only on the relevant sense and does not meet the word-level consensus threshold. Tatoeba examples remain sense-unverified.
notes.gossamer: Reviewed delicate/light or translucent adjective senses and noun senses for spider-web filaments and fine gauze. Simple's 'very weak' gloss is narrower/less precise, while its cobweb definition fits one noun use. The sky/cloud sentence is only a spelling match and may not describe spider silk.
notes.quixotic: The single OEWN adjective sense describes impractical idealism. The Tatoeba quest example is compatible with that sense on manual reading, but its stored status remains unverified_sense because the pipeline only checks word presence. There is no Simple gloss or topic label in the selected data.
notes.melancholy: Reviewed adjective senses for gloomy character and noun senses for sadness/temperament; Simple glosses describe the sad feeling and its effect. The historical bodily-humor definition is dated and should not be mistaken for current medical fact. Emotions and Science labels are sense-specific; the word has no consensus topic.
notes.obfuscate: The OEWN core is making something unclear. Simple glosses separately describe deliberate concealment through confusing language and obscuring code structure; these are useful domain-specific refinements, but no alignment was accepted. The two inspected Simple examples visibly illustrate their respective contexts; Tatoeba examples are not assigned to those senses.
notes.sublime: The adjective has elevated, extreme, and reverential senses, while the verb has the technical phase-change meaning. The Simple gloss about a solid becoming gas matches the technical verb, not the adjective. The Tatoeba examples use the adjective sense but remain marked unresolved by the database.
notes.mundane: OEWN distinguishes worldly/earthly from concern with ordinary worldly matters. Simple's 'not new' gloss is a questionable oversimplification and does not reliably express the common 'ordinary' sense; its example sentence suggests ordinary/unexciting life. Retain source attribution and consider editorial review before preferring that gloss.
notes.myriad: The adjective means too numerous to count; noun senses include a large indefinite number and a historical numeric value. Simple supports the large-quantity meaning but its wording is awkward. The Three produces myriad things sentence is a word match, not an automatically verified illustration of the count sense.
